Tertium: *de overgang van eigendom van e: Tertium: *the passing of ownership of a tangible movable under a contract* (typically: sale). Which acts are required, at what moment does ownership pass, and what follows if the underlying contract turns out to be void? Three models: **causal tradition system** (NL), **abstract tradition system** (DE) and **consensual system** (FR, *solo consensu*). The EU leaves the system of property ownership to the Member States (Art. 345 TFEU) and regulates only around the edges (passing of risk, conflict of laws).

## Trennungs- en Abstraktionsprinzip\nHe:
## Trennungs- and Abstraktionsprinzip
The BGB separates the **Verpflichtungsgeschäft** (the sale, § 433: obliges only to *übergeben und Eigentum verschaffen*) from the **Verfügungsgeschäft** (the transfer of ownership itself, §§ 929 ff.). That is the *Trennungsprinzip*. The *Abstraktionsprinzip* adds that the validity of the Verfügung **does not depend** on the validity of the Kausalgeschäft.

## Elements of § 929 sentence 1
1. **Einigung**: a real agreement aimed at passing ownership; subject to the general law of juridical acts (§§ 104 ff., 116 ff.).
2. **Übergabe**: complete surrender of possession by the transferor and acquisition of possession by the transferee (Realakt). Substitutes: § 929 sentence 2 (brevi manu), § 930 (Besitzkonstitut), § 931 (Abtretung des Herausgabeanspruchs).
3. **Einigsein** at the moment of Übergabe (until then the Einigung is freely revocable, unlike the obligational sale).
4. **Berechtigung** of the transferor; otherwise gutgläubiger Erwerb §§ 932–935 (not for *abhanden gekommene Sachen*, § 935).

## Consequence of a void sale
The transferee becomes owner; the transferor has only a **Bereicherungsanspruch** (§ 812(1) sentence 1 alt. 1, *Leistungskondiktion*) — a personal claim, weaker in insolvency and on resale. Corrections: *Fehleridentität* (the same defect of consent also affects the Einigung, e.g. § 123), *Bedingungszusammenhang* (§ 158: Einigung conditional on a valid sale) and *Geschäftseinheit* (§ 139, applied cautiously by the BGH).

## Comparative observation
Abstraction protects commerce (transferees need not investigate the title) at the expense of the transferor. NL and FR achieve third-party protection by another route: Art. 3:86 BW and Art. 2276 C. civ. protect the *subsequent* good-faith acquirer, without making the first transferee owner.
Geen Unieregel voor de eigendomsovergang: No EU rule on the passing of ownership itself (Art. 345 TFEU; Art. 4(b) CISG excludes it); around the edges: passing of risk in consumer sales (Art. 20 Directive 2011/83/EU) and the DCFR as a model (VIII.–2:101: consensual with a delivery requirement unless otherwise agreed).
## Bevoegdheidsvoorbehoud\nArt. 345 VWEU:
## Reservation of competence
Art. 345 TFEU shall ‘in no way prejudice the rules in Member States governing the system of property ownership’. The Court reads this narrowly (it does not exempt Member States from the fundamental freedoms), but the **mode of transfer of ownership** is undisputedly national. The Vienna Sales Convention (CISG, not EU law but in force in all three systems) likewise expressly does *not* govern, in Art. 4(b), ‘the effect which the contract may have on the property in the goods sold’.

## What the Union does regulate
- **Passing of risk** in consumer sales: Art. 20 Directive 2011/83/EU ties risk to the consumer’s *physical possession*, irrespective of the national ownership rule. This in effect harmonises the consequence where FR (*res perit domino*) and DE/NL (§ 446 BGB, Art. 7:10 BW: on delivery) diverge.
- **Conflict of laws**: the *lex rei sitae* is unwritten or nationally codified in all Member States (Art. 10:127 BW, Art. 43 EGBGB); the Union has not harmonised private international property law, unlike the law of obligations (Rome I).

## Soft law as tertium
The DCFR (Book VIII) opts in VIII.–2:101 for a **mixed model**: transfer requires a valid *underlying contract or other juridical act* (causal, like NL/FR), and in principle *delivery* (tradition, like NL/DE), but the parties may freely fix the moment (after FR). The DCFR is thus itself a comparative compromise and makes the three models clearly visible.

## Transfert solo consensu\nArt. 1196 al:
## Transfert solo consensu
Art. 1196 para. 1 (since 2016, previously Arts 1138 and 711) lays down the principle: in contracts *ayant pour objet l’aliénation de la propriété*, ownership passes *lors de la conclusion du contrat*. For sale, Art. 1583 repeats it: *la propriété est acquise de droit à l’acheteur … dès qu’on est convenu de la chose et du prix*. There is thus **no separate real act**; the contract is both title and mode (*effet translatif du contrat*).

## Role of délivrance
*Délivrance* (Art. 1604) is not a requirement for transfer but an **obligation of the seller** (*obligation de délivrer*, Art. 1603). Equating it with the Dutch ‘levering’ is a mistake: a classic faux ami.

## Corrections to consensualism
- *Choses de genre*: passing only on identification (Art. 1585 ff.; implicit in Art. 1196 para. 2, ‘la nature des choses’).
- *Clause de réserve de propriété* (Art. 2367 ff.): postponement ‘par la volonté des parties’.
- Risk follows ownership (*res perit domino*, Art. 1196 para. 3), save after notice of default.

## Third-party protection
Since ownership already passes with the contract, commerce must be protected against invisible transfers: Art. 1198 para. 1 (in a double sale, whoever first takes possession in good faith prevails) and Art. 2276 (possession of movables counts as title; revendication for three years in case of loss or theft). Both are functionally equivalent to Art. 3:86 BW and § 932 BGB, but systematically anchored in *possession*, not in the transfer.

## Nullity of the sale
The system is **causal**: *nullité* operates retroactively (Art. 1178), ownership never passed and is revindicated; *restitutions* under Art. 1352 ff. Here FR stands close to NL and opposite DE.
Causaal traditiestelsel: overdracht vere: Causal tradition system: transfer requires delivery (giving possession) under a valid title by a person entitled to dispose; if the title falls away, ownership never passed.
## Drie vereisten (art. 3:84 lid 1 BW)\n:
## Three requirements (Art. 3:84(1) BW)
1. **Valid title**: the legal relationship that justifies the transfer, usually the sale. Nullity or avoidance of the title (with retroactive effect, Art. 3:53) means that ownership *never* passed: the **causal system**. The transferor revindicates (Art. 5:2) and need not fall back on a personal claim for undue payment.
2. **Power to dispose**: in principle only the owner (nemo plus). Third-party protection via Art. 3:86 (movables, non-registered property: good-faith acquirer *other than gratuitously*).
3. **Delivery**: for movables under the transferor’s control, by *giving possession* (Art. 3:90(1)), which under Art. 3:114 can be done physically or via the three traditiones fictae of Art. 3:115 (brevi manu, constitutum possessorium, longa manu).

## Real agreement?
Whether a separate ‘real agreement’ is needed besides title and delivery is disputed (Meijers: yes, as part of delivery; cf. the German *Einigung*). Of practical relevance for defects of consent affecting only the act of delivery.

## Moment of passing
On delivery, not on sale. Until then the seller remains owner; in consumer sales risk passes only on delivery to the consumer (Art. 7:11).

## Comparative observation
NL sits between DE and FR: a separate act of delivery (unlike FR), but no abstraction (unlike DE). Art. 3:84(3) (ban on fiduciary transfer) shows that the *purpose* of the title matters in property law: a pure security purpose is not a valid title.
Culpa in contrahendo, gecodificeerd in §: Culpa in contrahendo, codified in § 311 II read with § 241 II and § 280 I BGB: the Aufnahme von Vertragsverhandlungen creates a (quasi-)contractual Schuldverhältnis with Rücksichtnahmepflichten; breaking off without triftigen Grund after inducing reliance obliges compensation of the reliance interest (Vertrauensschaden).
## Grondslag: gesetzliches Schuldverhält:
## Basis: gesetzliches Schuldverhältnis
Jhering (1861) developed *culpa in contrahendo*; the Reichsgericht accepted it in the **Linoleumrollen** case (RGZ 78, 239) as customary law based on § 242. The **Schuldrechtsmodernisierung 2002** codified it: § 311(2) creates a *Schuldverhältnis mit Pflichten nach § 241 Abs. 2* through (1) Aufnahme von Vertragsverhandlungen, (2) Anbahnung eines Vertrags, (3) ähnliche geschäftliche Kontakte. Doctrinally this is a **gesetzliches Schuldverhältnis ohne primäre Leistungspflicht**: contractual in structure (§ 278 vicarious liability, § 280 burden of proof), non-contractual in origin.

## Anspruchsgrundlage
§§ 280(1), 311(2), 241(2) BGB. Requirements: Schuldverhältnis (§ 311 II), Pflichtverletzung (breach of a Rücksichtnahmepflicht, § 241 II), Vertretenmüssen (presumed, § 280 I 2), Schaden.

## Abbruch von Vertragsverhandlungen
The starting point is **Abschlussfreiheit**: no one is obliged to contract, and whoever breaks off acts lawfully in principle, even if the other has incurred costs. There is a Pflichtverletzung only where a party (a) induced the belief that the contract would *certainly* be concluded (*Vertrauenstatbestand*) and (b) then breaks off *ohne triftigen Grund* (BGH NJW 1975, 1774; BGH NJW 1996, 1884). For **formbedürftige Verträge** (§ 311b: land) the bar is higher: only for *vorsätzlicher Treuepflichtverletzung* (BGH 29.03.1996, V ZR 332/94), since the form requirements would otherwise be hollowed out.

## Extent: negatives Interesse
Compensation covers the **Vertrauensschaden**: the injured party is put in the position as if it had never relied on the contract (wasted expenditure, missed alternative deals). The **Erfüllungsinteresse** is excluded, as there is no Abschlusspflicht; it may however serve as an *Obergrenze* (by analogy with § 122(1)). Here DE differs sharply from Plas/Valburg.

## Comparative observation
The contractual framing brings practical advantages (§ 278 instead of § 831, reversed burden of proof § 280 I 2, 30-year instead of 3-year limitation before 2002; now the same). FR and NL reach comparable results in tort; only the extent (NL) and the express exclusion of perte de chance (FR) differ.
Geen materiële Unieregel; wel een autono: No substantive EU rule; but an autonomous characterisation: precontractual liability is ‘non-contractual’ (CJEU Tacconi, Art. 7(2) Brussels I bis) and has its own conflict rule in Rome II (Art. 12: the lex contractus of the contract envisaged).
## Kwalificatie: autonoom en niet-contra:
## Characterisation: autonomous and non-contractual
In **Tacconi** (C-334/00) the Court held that a claim for precontractual liability, in the absence of *obligations freely assumed*, does not concern ‘matters relating to a contract’ (Art. 5(1) Brussels Convention) but ‘matters relating to tort, delict or quasi-delict’ (Art. 5(3), now Art. 7(2) Brussels I bis). That is remarkable against the German contractual framing: EU law here functionally follows the French and Dutch view.

## Conflict rule: Rome II Art. 12
Rome II (864/2007) expressly includes c.i.c. (Art. 2(1)) and gives it an **own rule** that corrects the tortious characterisation again: the applicable law is the law that governs or would have governed *the contract envisaged* (para. 1, *accessory connection*), alternatively the lex loci damni, the common habitual residence or the closest connection (para. 2). Recital 30 limits the concept to breach of disclosure duties and *breakdown of contractual negotiations*; personal injury during negotiations falls under Art. 4.

## Soft law
PECL Art. 2:301 and DCFR II.–3:301 state the common core: freedom to negotiate and to break off, liability for conduct *contrary to good faith and fair dealing*, in particular negotiating with no real intention of reaching an agreement. Both limit compensation to the loss caused by the breach (reliance interest) — closer to DE/FR than to Plas/Valburg.

## Comparative observation
The Union is not a fourth substantive system here but a **meta-level**: it imposes a common characterisation that neutralises the national doctrinal differences (contract/tort) for jurisdiction and applicable law.

## Grondslag: responsabilité délictuelle:
## Basis: responsabilité délictuelle
Before 2016, *rupture abusive des pourparlers* was purely judge-made law based on (old) Art. 1382. **Ordonnance 2016-131** codified it in Art. 1112, in the new *Sous-section 1 — Les négociations* of the chapter on contract formation. The characterisation remains **non-contractual**: there is no contract yet, so Art. 1240 (ex 1382) is the basis of liability; Art. 1112 supplies the standard of conduct and the limitation of damages.

## Standard: liberté et bonne foi
Art. 1112 para. 1 puts **freedom** first (*l’initiative, le déroulement et la rupture … sont libres*) and subjects it *impérativement* to **bonne foi** — the precontractual extension of Art. 1104 (*négociés, formés et exécutés de bonne foi*, d’ordre public). A faute is, for instance, abruptly breaking off after long negotiations without reason, parallel negotiations despite a promise of exclusivity, or carrying on without any real intention to contract (*pourparlers de pure forme*). A *motif légitime* excludes faute.

## Extent: Manoukian codified
**Cass. com. 26 Nov. 2003 (Manoukian)**: the loss caused by breaking off includes neither the benefits of the contract not concluded nor the *perte de chance* of obtaining them. Art. 1112 para. 2 adopted this; the 2018 ratification statute added — after criticism that the ordonnance left the perte de chance open — the words *ni la perte de chance d’obtenir ces avantages*. Recoverable are thus: costs incurred (études, frais de négociation), and possibly lost chances of *other* contracts.

## Accompanying duties
Art. 1112-1 (*devoir d’information*, d’ordre public) and Art. 1112-2 (*confidentialité*) complete the regime; breaching them is a faute in its own right.

## Comparative observation
FR is the most explicit on **extent**: even perte de chance is excluded, whereas DE sometimes allows it within the reliance interest and NL accepts the expectation interest in principle. On the **standard** the three converge: freedom as the starting point, liability for induced reliance followed by breaking off without good reason.
Ongeschreven recht, ontwikkeld door de H: Unwritten law, developed by the Hoge Raad: breaking off is free unless, in view of the other party’s justified reliance on the conclusion of the contract or the other circumstances, it is unacceptable (CBB/JPO); the expectation interest may then even be owed (Plas/Valburg).
## Basis
No statutory provision. Since **Baris/Riezenkamp** (1957) the Hoge Raad has placed the negotiation phase under *good faith*: parties entering into negotiations stand ‘in a special legal relationship governed by good faith’. The doctrinal basis is twofold: Art. 6:162 (tort) for liability, Arts 6:2/6:248 (reasonableness and fairness) for the standard. The draft Art. 6.5.2.8a that would have codified the doctrine never became law.

## Standard: from three phases to one strict test
**Plas/Valburg** (1982) produced the well-known *three-phase model*: (1) free to break off; (2) breaking off permitted, but costs owed; (3) breaking off unacceptable, possibly with compensation of lost profit. **CBB/JPO** (2005) summarised and tightened the standard: breaking off is free *unless* unacceptable because of justified reliance on the conclusion of the contract or other circumstances; the standard is ‘strict and calls for restraint’. Relevant: who contributed to the reliance, unforeseen circumstances and, in long negotiations, the moment of breaking off against the background of the whole.

## Extent
Unique in the comparison: in the third phase NL in principle accepts compensation of the **expectation interest** (lost profit), because the other party was entitled to rely on *a* contract being concluded. DE and FR limit themselves to the reliance interest. Since CBB/JPO the third phase is rarely reached; the practice is reimbursement of costs (second phase, now mostly via Art. 6:212 or 6:162).

## Comparative observation
Functionally NL is closest to DE (protection of reliance, good faith as the standard), but without the contractual framing of § 311 II and with the wider extent of damages. Against FR (Art. 1112 para. 2) the difference in extent is one of principle.

Key passage, paraphrased as usually cited in the literature.
A party may be prevented from departing: A party may be prevented from departing from an assumption it induced — that a contract would be concluded — where departure would be unconscionable; relief is proportionate to the detriment. Unlike English promissory estoppel it can found a cause of action. (not verified)
A person must not, in trade or commerce,: A person must not, in trade or commerce, engage in conduct that is misleading or deceptive or likely to mislead or deceive. Applies to pre-contractual negotiations, including silence and representations about future matters (s 4 ACL); no fault required. (not verified)
Modelled on the English Sale of Goods Ac: Modelled on the English Sale of Goods Act 1893: property in specific or ascertained goods passes when the parties intend it to pass, with statutory rules for ascertaining that intention. The same scheme applies in the other states. (not verified)
De feitelijke uitoefening van een recht: The factual exercise of a right as if one were its holder, directly or through a third party. Someone who holds a thing without behaving as holder of the right is a detentor; detention becomes possession only by conversion of title (Art. 3.20). (not verified)
Objectieve gedragsnorm: een contract moe: Objective standard of conduct: a contract must be performed in good faith (Art. 5.73), with supplementing and restricting effect; in the negotiation phase via Art. 5.15 and the duty of information in Art. 5.16. The prohibition of abuse of rights is laid down generally in Art. 1.10. (not verified)
Verbintenis van de verkoper om de verkoc: Obligation of the seller to place the thing sold in the control and possession of the buyer: performance of the sale, not a requirement for the passing of ownership, which already occurred by agreement. (not verified)
Wie onder bezwarende titel en te goeder: Whoever acquires for value and in good faith a real right in a movable from a person without power to dispose becomes holder as soon as he has undisturbed possession (Art. 3.28); the possessor in good faith is presumed to have title (Art. 3.24). Successor to Art. 2279 of the old Civil Code. (not verified)
De overdracht gebeurt door een rechtshan: Transfer takes place by a juridical act of transfer by a person with power to dispose, in performance of a valid title (obligation to give). That act is formed by mere agreement and is presumed to coincide with entering into the obligation; for generic goods only on specification, for future goods only once they come into existence. (not verified)
Partijen zijn vrij onderhandelingen aan: Parties are free to enter into, conduct and break off negotiations, but act in good faith (Art. 5.15). Liability is non-contractual (Art. 5.17(1)). For wrongful breaking off: restoration to the position without negotiations; where there was legitimate reliance that the contract would be concluded beyond any doubt, also the expected net benefits (Art. 5.17(2)). (not verified)
Wer die tatsächliche Gewalt über eine Sa: Whoever has actual control over a thing is its possessor. Independent (owner) and dependent possession (e.g. the tenant): both are possessors (Art. 920). (not verified)
Zur Übertragung des Fahrniseigentums bed: Transfer of ownership of movables requires transfer of possession: handing over the thing or the means giving control over it (Art. 922); transfer by instruction and constitutum possessorium as substitutes (Art. 924). (not verified)
Die Übertragung des Fahrniseigentums set: Transfer of ownership of movables requires, besides the transfer of possession, a valid legal ground. Unlike Germany, the causal principle applies (BGE 55 II 302); for land expressly Art. 974(2) ZGB. (not verified)
Jedermann hat in der Ausübung seiner Rec: Every person must act in good faith in the exercise of his rights and in the performance of his obligations (Art. 2(1)); the manifest abuse of a right is not protected by law (para. 2). Distinct from good faith in Art. 3. (not verified)
Haftung für die Verletzung vorvertraglic: Liability for breach of precontractual duties arising from the relationship of trust created by negotiations (Art. 2 ZGB). Not codified; the Federal Supreme Court classifies it as a reliance liability of its own kind between contract and tort. Compensation in principle of the reliance interest. (not verified)
Wer eine bewegliche Sache in gutem Glaub: Whoever receives a movable in good faith as owner becomes owner even if the transferor was not entitled to dispose, provided the thing had been entrusted to him (Art. 933); lost or stolen things may be reclaimed for five years (Art. 934). (not verified)
Ersatz des aus dem Dahinfallen des Vertr: Compensation for the loss resulting from the contract falling away: the injured party is to be put in the position as if it had never relied on the contract (Art. 26(1) CO for negligent mistake, Art. 39(1) CO for an agent without authority). (not verified)
Grundsatz, dass die Wirksamkeit des Verf: Principle that the validity of the dispositive act is independent of the validity of the underlying obligational act. Complements the Trennungsprinzip. Corrections: Fehleridentität, Bedingungszusammenhang, § 139.
Die tatsächliche Gewalt über eine Sache,: Actual control over a thing, regardless of the intention to hold it as one’s own: the tenant too is a possessor (for another). Distinction between possession for oneself/for another (§ 872), direct/indirect possession (§ 868).
Der auf den Eigentumsübergang gerichtete: The real agreement aimed at passing ownership. Abstract from the Kausalgeschäft; freely revocable until Übergabe; subject to the general rules on declarations of intent.
Das schuldrechtliche Verpflichtungsgesch: The obligational act that forms the legal ground (causa) for the Verfügung. By virtue of the Abstraktionsprinzip not a condition of validity of the transfer; its absence gives rise only to the Leistungskondiktion.
Objektiver Verhaltensmaßstab (Generalkla: Objective standard of conduct (general clause) for the content and exercise of rights and duties. To be strictly distinguished from good faith in the subjective sense (§ 932: gutgläubig).
Haftung für die schuldhafte Verletzung v: Liability for culpable breach of Rücksichtnahmepflichten arising from the statutory obligation created by entering into negotiations. Compensation of the reliance interest (Vertrauensschaden); freedom not to contract is preserved.
Der Schaden, den der Geschädigte dadurch: The loss the injured party suffers by having relied on the conclusion of the contract: it is to be put in the position as if it had never relied. Counterpart: Erfüllungsinteresse (expectation interest).
Realakt: vollständige Aufgabe des Besitz: Physical act: complete surrender of possession by the transferor and acquisition of possession by the transferee (or a person designated by him). Second element of transfer alongside the Einigung; replaceable by §§ 930, 931.
Voluntary transfer of possession from on: Voluntary transfer of possession from one person to another (s 61(1)). The seller's duty to deliver (s 27) is a contractual obligation, not a requirement for the passing of property. (not verified)
No general organising principle of good: No general organising principle of good faith in English contract law. A duty may be implied in 'relational' contracts as a matter of construction; statutory good faith in consumer law (unfair terms, s 62 CRA 2015). (not verified)
A false statement of fact or law inducin: A false statement of fact or law inducing a contract. Damages under s 2(1) are assessed on the tort (deceit) measure — reliance, not expectation — unless the representor proves reasonable belief in its truth. (not verified)
A buyer acquires no better title than th: A buyer acquires no better title than the seller had (s 21(1)), subject to closed exceptions: estoppel, mercantile agents, sale under a voidable title, seller or buyer in possession (ss 23–25). No general protection of the good-faith purchaser. (not verified)
English law recognises no general duty t: English law recognises no general duty to negotiate in good faith: an agreement to negotiate is unenforceable for uncertainty and each party may withdraw at any time. Protection is piecemeal: misrepresentation, collateral contract, restitution for work requested in anticipation of a contract, estoppel. (not verified)
In a sale of specific or ascertained goo: In a sale of specific or ascertained goods, property passes when the parties intend it to pass (s 17); absent a contrary intention the rules in s 18 apply (Rule 1: unconditional contract for specific goods in a deliverable state — on conclusion of the contract). No property passes in unascertained goods until they are ascertained (s 16). (not verified)
Factual control coupled with an intentio: Factual control coupled with an intention to possess. Possession is itself a root of title (relativity of title) and is protected by conversion and trespass to goods; a bailee is in possession. (not verified)
Wasted expenditure incurred in reliance: Wasted expenditure incurred in reliance on the contract, recoverable as an alternative to expectation loss, including pre-contractual expenditure within the parties' contemplation; capped by what the claimant would have earned. (not verified)
Los derechos deben ejercitarse conforme: Rights must be exercised in accordance with the requirements of good faith (Art. 7.1); contracts also bind to the consequences which, according to their nature, are in keeping with good faith (Art. 1258). (not verified)
Sin regulación específica: la ruptura in: No specific rule: unjustified breaking off of preliminary negotiations that disappoints the reliance induced is brought under non-contractual liability (Art. 1902), founded on good faith (Art. 7.1). The reliance interest is compensated. (not verified)
La posesión de los bienes muebles, adqui: Possession of movables acquired in good faith is equivalent to title; whoever lost the thing or was unlawfully deprived of it may reclaim it. Scope disputed (Romanist or Germanist reading). (not verified)
Posesión natural: la tenencia de una cos: Natural possession: holding a thing or enjoying a right; civil possession: that same holding combined with the intention of having the thing as one’s own. (not verified)
La propiedad se transmite por consecuenc: Ownership is transferred as a consequence of certain contracts by means of tradition (Art. 609): the contract (title) is not enough, delivery (mode) is needed; the creditor acquires no real right until delivery (Art. 1095). Causal system: nullity of the title prevents transfer. (not verified)
Se entiende entregada la cosa vendida cu: The thing sold is deemed delivered when it is placed in the control and possession of the buyer; spiritualised forms are allowed, such as executing a public deed (Art. 1462.2). It is the ‘mode’ that completes the transfer. (not verified)
Autonomous notion: non-contractual oblig: Autonomous notion: non-contractual obligation arising out of dealings prior to the conclusion of a contract, covering violation of the duty of disclosure and the breakdown of negotiations. Governed by the (putative) lex contractus.
Ownership of goods passes if the goods e: Ownership of goods passes if the goods exist and are transferable, the transferor has the right or authority to transfer, the transferee is entitled to it under a contract or other juridical act, and the parties agree on the time or — by default — the goods are delivered. Causal: if the underlying act is invalid, ownership is treated as never having passed (VIII.-2:202). (not verified)
Notion à double sens : (i) norme objecti: A notion with two meanings: (i) objective standard of fair dealing in the negotiation, formation and performance of the contract (Art. 1104); (ii) the possessor’s mistaken but legitimate belief (Arts 2274, 550), presumed. French does not distinguish the two lexically.
Le transport de la chose vendue en la pu: The transport of the thing sold into the control and possession of the buyer: performance of an obligation of the seller (Art. 1603), with no effect on the passing of ownership, which takes place solo consensu.
La disparition actuelle et certaine d'un: The present and certain disappearance of a favourable prospect. Recoverable in principle in French law, but expressly excluded for breaking off negotiations (loss of the chance of obtaining the benefits of the contract).
La détention ou la jouissance d'une chos: The holding or enjoyment of a thing that we hold or exercise ourselves, or through another who holds or exercises it in our name: corpus and animus domini. The détenteur précaire (tenant) is not a possessor (Art. 2266).
Responsabilité extracontractuelle pour f: Non-contractual liability for fault in conducting or breaking off negotiations, in breach of bonne foi (Art. 1112 para. 1). Limited compensation: neither the benefits expected from the contract nor the chance of obtaining them (Art. 1112 para. 2).
Dans la maxime « en fait de meubles, la: In the maxim ‘en fait de meubles, la possession vaut titre’, titre means proof of ownership (justification of the right), not a causa of transfer: possession in good faith relieves the possessor of proving the acquisition.
Le transfert de propriété d'un corps cer: Ownership of a specific thing passes by mere exchange of consents, on conclusion of the contract (Art. 1196 para. 1), without tradition; the parties may postpone it (retention of title). Délivrance is merely the performance of an obligation of the seller. (not verified)
Buona fede in senso oggettivo: regola di: Good faith in the objective sense: rule of conduct in negotiations (Art. 1337), interpretation (Art. 1366) and performance of the contract (Art. 1375), equivalent to the correttezza of Art. 1175. Distinct from subjective good faith (unawareness of infringing another’s right, Art. 1147). (not verified)
Obbligazione principale del venditore (a: Main obligation of the seller (Art. 1476 no. 1): to deliver the thing in the condition it was in at the time of sale. Not a requirement for the passing of ownership of a specific thing. (not verified)
Nei contratti che hanno per oggetto il t: In contracts whose object is the transfer of ownership of a specific thing, ownership is transferred and acquired by the lawfully expressed consent of the parties (consensual principle, in the wake of the Code civil). (not verified)
Il danno subito per aver confidato nella: The loss suffered by relying on the conclusion or validity of the contract: wasted expenditure and lost alternative opportunities; excludes the positive interest in performance. (not verified)
Il potere sulla cosa che si manifesta in: Power over a thing manifested in activity corresponding to the exercise of ownership or another real right. Whoever holds the thing for another (tenant, depositary) is a detentore, not a possessor. (not verified)
Chi riceve beni mobili da un non proprie: Whoever receives movables from a non-owner acquires ownership through possession, provided he is in good faith at the time of delivery and there is a title capable of transferring ownership. (not verified)
Le parti, nello svolgimento delle tratta: In conducting negotiations and forming the contract, the parties must behave in good faith (Art. 1337). Nature disputed: non-contractual (Art. 2043) according to traditional case law, arising from ‘qualified social contact’ (contractual) according to Cass. 14188/2016. Compensation of the reliance interest. (not verified)
Het houden van een goed voor zichzelf. W: Holding a thing for oneself. Whoever holds for another is a holder (houder), not a possessor (Arts 3:107(4), 3:108).
De geldigheid van de overdracht hangt af: The validity of the transfer depends on the validity of the title. Nullity or avoidance of the title means that no ownership passed; the transferor revindicates.
De rechtshandeling waardoor, krachtens t: The juridical act by which, under a title, the transfer is completed; for movables, giving possession (Arts 3:90, 3:114, 3:115). Comprises both the physical act and (according to the prevailing view) the real agreement.
De schade die bestaat in het verschil tu: The loss consisting in the difference between the actual financial position and that in which the injured party would have been had the contract been concluded and performed (lost profit). Recoverable in principle in the third phase of Plas/Valburg.
Rechtersrechtelijke figuur: aansprakelij: Judge-made doctrine: liability for breaking off negotiations where, in view of the other party’s justified reliance or the other circumstances, that is unacceptable. May lead to compensation of the expectation interest.
Objectieve gedragsnorm (de 'goede trouw': Objective standard of conduct (the ‘good faith’ in the objective sense of the old BW) with supplementing and derogating effect. To be distinguished from subjective good faith in Art. 3:11 (not knowing and not being required to know).
De rechtsverhouding die de overdracht re: The legal relationship that justifies the transfer (iusta causa traditionis), usually the obligational contract. Requirement for a valid transfer: causal system.
Every contract imposes upon each party a: Every contract imposes upon each party a duty of good faith and fair dealing in its performance and its enforcement — not in its negotiation (Rest. 2d § 205 cmt. c). (not verified)
A person with voidable title can transfe: A person with voidable title can transfer good title to a good-faith purchaser for value (§ 2-403(1)); entrusting goods to a merchant who deals in goods of that kind gives him power to transfer all rights of the entruster to a buyer in ordinary course of business (§ 2-403(2)). (not verified)
Title passes in any manner and on any co: Title passes in any manner and on any conditions explicitly agreed; otherwise at the time and place at which the seller completes performance with reference to physical delivery (§ 2-401(2)). Article 2 deliberately makes most rights and remedies independent of where title lies. (not verified)
A promise which the promisor should reas: A promise which the promisor should reasonably expect to induce action or forbearance, and which does induce it, is binding if injustice can be avoided only by enforcement. Hoffman v Red Owl applied it to failed negotiations and awarded reliance damages. (not verified)
Übergabe is alleen de feitelijke handeli: Übergabe is only the physical act (Realakt); Dutch levering also includes the agreement, which in DE counts as the separate Einigung. Übergabe + Einigung ≈ levering.
Délivrance is uitvoering van een verbint: Délivrance is the performance of an obligation of the seller and has no proprietary effect; ownership has already passed solo consensu. Levering is constitutive in NL.
Beide betekenen 'overgave', maar Übergab: Both mean ‘handing over’, but Übergabe is a requirement for transfer, délivrance merely a contractual obligation.
De goederenrechtelijke overeenkomst zit: In NL the real agreement is hidden within delivery; in DE it is a free-standing dinglicher Vertrag.
Inhoudelijk dezelfde figuur (de causa),: Substantively the same concept (the causa), but in NL a condition of validity (causal), in DE not (abstract).
In art. 2276 betekent 'titre' eigendomsb: In Art. 2276 ‘titre’ means proof of ownership/legal ground of possession, not the iusta causa traditionis of Art. 3:84 BW.
Tegengestelde beginselen; NL heeft bewus: Opposite principles; NL deliberately chose the causal system (Meijers).
NL bezit vereist houden voor zichzelf (a: Dutch possession requires holding for oneself (animus domini); German Besitz is mere actual control, the tenant too is a Besitzer. Dutch ‘houderschap’ ≈ German ‘Fremdbesitz’.
Beide eisen corpus én animus domini; de: Both require corpus and animus domini; the holder (houder/détenteur précaire) is not a possessor.
FR possession vereist animus domini; DE: French possession requires animus domini; German Besitz does not. The French détenteur précaire is a Besitzer in DE.
Zelfde functie (vertrouwensbescherming b: Same function (protecting reliance when negotiations are broken off), but in NL unwritten and tortious, in DE codified and quasi-contractual; NL allows the expectation interest, DE does not.
Beide delictueel van grondslag; FR sluit: Both tortious in basis; FR expressly excludes perte de chance and the benefits of the contract, whereas NL allows lost profit in the third phase.
DE: Schuldverhältnis met Rücksichtnahmep: DE: Schuldverhältnis with Rücksichtnahmepflichten (§ 311 II); FR: responsabilité délictuelle (Art. 1240) with a statutory standard of conduct (Art. 1112). In both, the extent is limited to the reliance interest.
Rome II gebruikt de Duitse term maar kwa: Rome II uses the German term but characterises the doctrine as non-contractual (Tacconi), contrary to German doctrine.
De autonome EU-notie dekt het Nederlands: The autonomous EU notion fully covers the Dutch case (breaking off negotiations); Recital 30 mentions it expressly.
FR kwalificeert eveneens delictueel; art: FR also characterises it as tortious; Art. 12 Rome II departs from the lex loci damni only as regards the applicable law.
Beide objectieve gedragsnormen met aanvu: Both objective standards of conduct with supplementing and restricting effect; § 242 is historically the model for Arts 6:2/6:248.
FR 'bonne foi' omvat zowel de objectieve: French ‘bonne foi’ covers both the objective standard (Art. 1104) and subjective good faith (Art. 2276); NL separates reasonableness and fairness (objective) from good faith (subjective, Art. 3:11).
DE scheidt Treu und Glauben (§ 242) lexi: German distinguishes Treu und Glauben (§ 242) lexically from guter Glaube (§ 932); French uses ‘bonne foi’ for both.
Tegengestelde schadebegrippen: NL aanvaa: Opposite notions of loss: NL accepts the expectation interest in the third phase, DE limits c.i.c. to the reliance interest.
De perte de chance kan in DE onder het n: In DE perte de chance may fall within the reliance interest (missed alternative deal); in FR it is excluded for rupture des pourparlers insofar as it concerns the benefits of the contract.
Art. 1112 al. 2 sluit precies uit wat Pl: Art. 1112 para. 2 excludes precisely what Plas/Valburg allows: the benefits (or chance of benefits) of the contract not concluded.
FR kent geen levering als overdrachtsver: FR does not require delivery for transfer: ownership passes solo consensu; NL requires delivery under a valid title. (not verified)
Zelfde uitkomst (overgang bij wilsoveree: Same outcome (passing by agreement), but since 2021 BE expressly distinguishes the title (obligation to give) from the juridical act of transfer. (not verified)
Art. 1376 c.c. volgt het Franse consensu: Art. 1376 c.c. follows French consensualism: passing by agreement for a specific thing. (not verified)
Geen van beide eist levering. FR: overga: Neither requires delivery. FR: passing on conclusion of the contract; EN: when the parties intend, with s 18 Rule 1 as a presumption of passing on conclusion of the contract. (not verified)
Beide causaal en met een traditio-vereis: Both causal and with a tradition requirement; ES accepts spiritualised forms (a notarial deed as delivery, Art. 1462.2 CC). (not verified)
Spanje wijkt bewust af van het Franse co: Spain deliberately departs from French consensualism: title alone does not transfer. (not verified)
Spanje is causaal: zonder geldige titel: Spain is causal: without a valid title no passing of ownership. (not verified)
Beide: overdracht vereist een geldige re: Both: transfer requires a valid legal ground and giving possession. (not verified)
Het ZGB nam de Duitse structuur (Besitzü: The ZGB took over the German structure (Besitzübergang) but rejected the Abstraktionsprinzip (BGE 55 II 302). (not verified)
Zelfde Realakt met dezelfde surrogaten (: The same Realakt with the same substitutes (Besitzanweisung, Besitzkonstitut). (not verified)
CH Besitzübergang is het feitelijke deel: Swiss Besitzübergang is the physical part of Dutch levering; in CH the agreement lies in the Verfügungsgeschäft. (not verified)
Beide constitutief (modo), maar de tradi: Both constitutive (modo), but the tradición instrumental (Art. 1462.2 CC) goes further than Dutch giving of possession. (not verified)
Zelfde betekenis 'overgave', maar in ES: Same meaning of ‘handing over’, but in ES a requirement for passing ownership, in FR merely performance of the sale. (not verified)
Beide: verbintenis van de verkoper, zond: Both: an obligation of the seller, with no proprietary effect for a specific thing. (not verified)
Consegna is uitvoering van de koop; de N: Consegna is performance of the sale; Dutch levering is a requirement for transfer. (not verified)
Art. 1604 oud BW is dezelfde bepaling al: Art. 1604 of the old Belgian Civil Code is the same provision as Art. 1604 C. civ. (not verified)
Zelfde woord in dezelfde taal, ander beg: Same word in the same language, different concept: in BE an obligation of the seller, in NL the juridical act that transfers ownership. (not verified)
Delivery is in EN alleen een contractuel: In EN delivery is only a contractual duty (s 27 SGA); property passes according to the parties’ intention. (not verified)
Beide: overdracht van het bezit als uitv: Both: transfer of possession as performance of the sale, separate from the passing of ownership. (not verified)
Beide volgen in de eerste plaats de wil: Both follow first and foremost the parties’ intention; absent agreement, title passes in the US on delivery (§ 2-401(2)), property in EN for specific goods already on conclusion of the contract. (not verified)
De Australische Sale of Goods Acts nemen: The Australian Sale of Goods Acts adopt the English scheme of 1893. (not verified)
Het DCFR is causaal en eist standaard le: The DCFR is causal and requires delivery by default, but lets the parties choose another moment. (not verified)
Het DCFR kiest uitdrukkelijk voor het ca: The DCFR expressly opts for the causal system (VIII.-2:202). (not verified)
Beide eisen uitoefening als rechthebbend: Both require exercise as holder of the right; the Belgian detentor is the Dutch houder. (not verified)
Art. 3.18 BW moderniseert dezelfde Frans: Art. 3.18 of the Belgian Civil Code modernises the same French concept (corpus and animus). (not verified)
Beide: macht over de zaak met animus dom: Both: power over the thing with animus domini; the detentore is not a possessore. (not verified)
IT onderscheidt possesso van detenzione;: IT distinguishes possesso from detenzione; in DE the tenant too is a Besitzer. (not verified)
De posesión natural (louter houden) ligt: Posesión natural (mere holding) is close to German Besitz; posesión civil (with animus) to Eigenbesitz. (not verified)
Beide zuiver feitelijke macht; selbständ: Both purely actual control; selbständiger/unselbständiger Besitz ≈ Eigen-/Fremdbesitz. (not verified)
De CH-huurder is Besitzer (Art. 920 ZGB): The Swiss tenant is a Besitzer (Art. 920 ZGB); in NL he is a holder, not a possessor. (not verified)
EN possession eist geen animus domini (o: English possession does not require animus domini (a bailee possesses too), but protects possession as a relative title. (not verified)
Art. 3.28 BW vervangt art. 2279 oud BW,: Art. 3.28 of the Belgian Civil Code replaces Art. 2279 of the old Civil Code, which was identical to Art. 2276 C. civ. (not verified)
Zelfde maxime; IT eist daarnaast uitdruk: Same maxim; IT additionally expressly requires a titolo idoneo. (not verified)
Zelfde maxime, maar de draagwijdte van a: Same maxim, but the scope of Art. 464 CC (acquisition or mere proof) is disputed. (not verified)
Beide beschermen de verkrijger te goeder: Both protect the good-faith acquirer of movables; CH expressly distinguishes entrusted from lost or stolen things. (not verified)
EN beschermt de verkrijger te goeder tro: EN protects the good-faith acquirer only in closed exceptions; FR makes possession in good faith the main rule. (not verified)
Zelfde vertrekpunt (nemo dat), maar de U: Same starting point (nemo dat), but the UCC entrustment rule is a wider exception than the English mercantile agent. (not verified)
Art. 5.17 BW codificeert in wezen de NL: Art. 5.17 of the Belgian Civil Code essentially codifies the Dutch three-phase doctrine (Plas/Valburg): reliance interest and, where there was justified reliance on conclusion, the expectation interest too. But non-contractual. (not verified)
Beide buitencontractueel; BE staat uitzo: Both non-contractual; BE exceptionally allows the expected net benefits, which Art. 1112 para. 2 C. civ. specifically excludes. (not verified)
De BE-kwalificatie (buitencontractueel): The Belgian characterisation (non-contractual) is in line with Art. 12 Rome II. (not verified)
Zelfde functie; art. 1337 c.c. is een ui: Same function; Art. 1337 c.c. is an express good-faith rule, its nature (contractual or not) is disputed in IT. (not verified)
Beide beperken de vergoeding tot het neg: Both limit compensation to the reliance interest; IT has its own provision, FR since 2016 Art. 1112. (not verified)
Voor de verwijzing kwalificeert art. 12: For the connecting factor, Art. 12 Rome II characterises autonomously, regardless of the Italian debate on contatto sociale. (not verified)
Beide delictueel via de algemene schadec: Both tortious via the general liability clause (Art. 1902 CC / Art. 1240 C. civ.). (not verified)
Zelfde term, andere grondslag: in ES del: Same term, different basis: in ES tortious, in DE a quasi-contractual Schuldverhältnis (§ 311(2) BGB). (not verified)
Zelfde naam en functie; CH ongecodificee: Same name and function; in CH uncodified and treated as Vertrauenshaftung sui generis, in DE codified in § 311(2) BGB. (not verified)
EN kent geen aansprakelijkheid voor het: EN has no liability for breaking off negotiations as such. (not verified)
Waar FR de vrijheid van onderhandelen be: Where FR limits the freedom to negotiate by bonne foi, EN leaves that freedom unlimited (Walford v Miles). (not verified)
Functioneel equivalent voor vertrouwenss: Functional equivalent for reliance loss when negotiations are broken off (Hoffman v Red Owl), but via a promise rather than good faith. (not verified)
Beide kunnen als zwaard dienen; AU bindt: Both can be used as a sword; AU ties it to unconscionability and limits relief to what the detriment requires. (not verified)
S 18 ACL gaat verder dan misrepresentati: S 18 ACL goes further than misrepresentation: no fault required, and silence and statements about the future are covered too. (not verified)
BE houdt de oude term 'goede trouw' aan: BE keeps the old term ‘good faith’ for what NL has called ‘reasonableness and fairness’ since 1992. (not verified)
Zelfde Franse traditie; BE heeft de norm: Same French tradition; BE has elaborated the standard further in Book 5 and Art. 1.10. (not verified)
Beide kennen de objectieve en de subject: Both know objective and subjective good faith under one word; IT also uses correttezza. (not verified)
Objectieve buona fede/correttezza ≈ Treu: Objective buona fede/correttezza ≈ Treu und Glauben (§ 242 BGB). (not verified)
Beide: objectieve norm voor uitoefening: Both: an objective standard for the exercise of rights and the content of contracts. (not verified)
Art. 2 ZGB is als algemene norm van het: Art. 2 ZGB, as a general rule for the whole of private law, is formulated even more broadly than § 242 BGB. (not verified)
